gloss: to top up; to add more; to replenish

definitions.gloss: to top up; to add more; to replenish
definitions.explanation: To pour or add more of a liquid or substance to something that is running low.

examples.english: I topped up the hot water.

examples.japanese: ⟦グラス→グラス：00076_gurasu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{空|から}→空：27640_kara⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なり→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦かけた→かける：00854_kakeru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦ワイン→ワイン：01067_wain⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{注|つ}ぎ{足|た}した。
examples.english: The glass was almost empty, so I poured more wine.

examples.japanese: ⟦スープ→スープ：00395_suupu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{少|すく}なく→少ない：01136_sukunai⟧⟦なって→なる：01970_naru⟧きたら、⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{注|つ}ぎ{足|た}し⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{煮込|にこ}んで→煮込む：05822_nikomu⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: If the soup starts running low, simmer it while adding more water.

notes:
A compound verb combining ⟦{注|つ}ぐ→注ぐ：02470_tsugu⟧ (to pour) and ⟦{足|た}す→足す：01168_tasu⟧ (to add, supplement). Specifically describes the action of replenishing a liquid or substance that has been partially consumed or reduced. Very common in cooking and dining contexts.

USAGE:
- Primarily used for liquids: water, soup, oil, beverages
- Implies the container already has some of the substance — you are adding more
- In Japanese dining culture, it is polite to {注|つ}ぎ{足|た}す drinks for others before they run out

TRANSITIVITY: Transitive (takes ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦お{湯|ゆ}→お湯：02518_oyu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{注|つ}ぎ{足|た}す: to top up hot water
- ⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{注|つ}ぎ{足|た}す: to add more water
- ⟦{油|あぶら}→油：01693_abura⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{注|つ}ぎ{足|た}す: to top up the oil
- ⟦ビール→ビール：01015_biiru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{注|つ}ぎ{足|た}す: to pour more beer

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{足|た}す→足す：01168_tasu⟧: to add — more general; not limited to pouring
- ⟦{注|つ}ぐ→注ぐ：02470_tsugu⟧: to pour — the base verb; simply pouring, not specifically replenishing
- ⟦{補充|ほじゅう}する→補充する：25240_hojuusuru⟧: to replenish, restock — more formal; used for supplies and inventory
- ⟦おかわり→おかわり：10967_okawari⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to have another serving — from the recipient's perspective; asking for more
